mechanism_log: The system has a mostly additive structure with one key interaction. ALL six inputs increase Y1 (with varying strengths). Y2 is decreased by X1,X2,X3,X4 but increased by X5,X6 — creating the core Y1-vs-Y2 trade-off. Y3 is driven by only X1 (saturating increase) and X3 (nonmonotonic peak near 0.55), with a meaningful X1*X3 interaction (X3 must be in ~0.3-0.8 for X1 to activate Y3). Y4 is driven mainly by X2 and X4, with moderate X3 contribution. X5 is a pure Y1 driver with Y2 penalty. X6 similarly increases Y1 but also increases Y2 and slightly hurts Y4. X4 is the most universally beneficial input (Y1↑, Y2↓, Y4↑, Y3 neutral). The X5*X4 interaction test confirmed perfect additivity (std=0.0), suggesting most of the system is additive except for the Y3 nonlinearity.

The system is predominantly additive with 6 inputs driving 4 outputs. ALL six inputs positively affect Y1 (with X5 and X1 being strongest). Y2 is decreased by X1, X2, X3, X4 (cooperative inputs) and increased by X5, X6 (conflict inputs), creating the core Pareto trade-off. Y3 is driven only by X1 (saturating increase) and X3 (nonmonotonic peak near 0.55-0.65), with a significant X1*X3 interaction — X3 must be in ~0.3-0.8 for X1 to activate Y3. Y4 is driven by X2, X4, and X3 (all positive), with X6 weakly negative and X5 having zero effect. The optimal strategy sets cooperative inputs to maximum (X1=1, X2=1, X3≈0.65, X4=1) and traces the Pareto front by varying X5 (primary trade-off lever) and X6 (secondary). This structure was confirmed by massive Pareto improvement: hypervolume nearly tripled from 0.407 to 1.156. Prediction accuracy reached <2% error on all outputs in final evaluations.

new_findings: X5 is a pure Y1/Y2 driver: strong Y1 increase (+0.649), moderate Y2 increase (+0.135), zero effect on Y3 and Y4. The Y2 gradient is exactly 0.15 everywhere — perfectly linear.
X4 is universally beneficial: increases Y1 (+0.457), strongly decreases Y2 (-0.249), increases Y4 (+0.202), no Y3 effect.
X3 has a NONMONOTONIC effect on Y3: Y3=0 at X3=0.1, peaks at ~0.90 near X3=0.55, drops to 0.33 at X3=1.0. This hump shape is critical for the Y3≥0.4 constraint.
X1 is the strongest Y3 driver (range 0.788) with saturating behavior, but X1 only activates Y3 when X3 is in the right range (~0.3-0.8). Confirmed by X1*X3 interaction test (std=0.146 on Y3).
X1*X3 interaction on Y3 is significant (std=0.146), but all other tested interactions are essentially zero. The system is largely additive except for Y3.
Gradients change substantially across the input space: X2→Y1 varies from 0.14 to 0.97, X1→Y1 from 0.34 to 0.90, indicating nonlinear main effects even without interactions.
X2 has zero effect on Y3 (confirmed by OAT sweep and gradients at multiple points).
surprises: X4 had a much stronger effect on Y1 than expected from correlations. OAT range was 0.457 — I predicted ~0.15 (flat). The correlation (0.15) was misleading because X4 was confounded with other variables in the initial data.
X3→Y3 is nonmonotonic (hump-shaped), not monotonically increasing as the positive correlation (0.63) suggested. At X3=1.0, Y3 drops to 0.33 which violates the ≥0.4 constraint.
X1→Y3 effect was much larger than predicted (range 0.788 vs predicted 0.3). X1 is THE critical input for Y3 feasibility.
X6 has zero effect on Y3, contradicting the initial negative correlation (-0.33) which was spurious.
X5*X4 interaction was exactly zero on all outputs — the system is more additive than expected.
iteration_summaries.next_plan: With 21 evaluations remaining, I should: (1) Test X2*X6 or X1*X5 interaction to check if the Y1 nonlinearity involves pairwise couplings, (2) Run a regression fit to quantify the functional forms, (3) Begin targeted Pareto optimization — evaluate promising corners like high X1/X2/X3~0.5/X4=1.0 with varying X5/X6 to explore the Y1-Y2 trade-off frontier while keeping Y3≥0.4.

X3=0.65 strictly dominates X3=0.50 in the cooperative-max regime: it gives better Y3 (0.987 vs 0.957), better Y4 (0.521 vs 0.501), and slightly better Y2, with negligible Y1 difference.

The Y1 range at cooperative-max spans 1.07 to 2.39 — far larger than any prior observation (max was 1.48). The system's full potential was hidden because cooperative inputs weren't simultaneously maximized.
Y2 coefficient for X5 is exactly 0.15 across the entire input space — perfectly linear with zero interactions. Confirmed by identical gradients at 3 different operating points.

The Pareto front is effectively 1-dimensional: once cooperative inputs are fixed at optimal values, only X5 (and secondarily X6) control the Y1↔Y2 trade-off. Y4 is essentially constant (~0.50) along the front.
Model calibration improved dramatically — final predictions had errors of 0.001-0.019 on all outputs, confirming the additive linear structure.
All 8 Pareto-optimal points have Y3 > 0.95, providing large safety margin on the ≥0.4 constraint.
surprises: Y2 can go NEGATIVE at cooperative-max configuration. The linear regression predicted Y2 ≈ -0.07, which was confirmed. Previous observations never showed Y2 < 0.09.

Y1 at cooperative-max with X5=1, X6=1 reaches 2.39 — far beyond the previous best of 1.48. The magnitude of Y1 was much larger than the linear model predicted from center-point gradients due to nonlinear amplification at high cooperative input values.

X3=0.65 gives HIGHER Y3 than X3=0.50 (0.987 vs 0.957) despite the hump-shaped response — the peak of Y3 vs X3 shifts rightward when X1 is at 1.0, confirming the X1*X3 interaction changes the optimal X3 location.

X4 had much stronger Y1 effect (+0.457 OAT range) than initial correlations suggested (r=0.15). This was the biggest screening surprise — confounding in the initial random data masked X4's true importance.
